solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Promote shoe from East so plugging slogan

parts.note: to back a cause is to promote or support it

indicators.note: one piece plugs a gap in the other, sitting inside it
in an across clue, coming from the East means reading right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A shoe retailer's marketing pitch, with Eastern stock being pushed hard under a catchy line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from East' turns the clog round to read TOBAS. 'so' is the Latin SIC, as printed after a quoted error.
explanation.definitionFit: Back to Basics was the political slogan of John Major's Conservative government in the 1990s.

clue.text: Flattering talk in past about Latin composer

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: by can mean past, as in walk by
Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: Smooth words once spoken about a Latin composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Blarney is smooth, charming flattery, named after the Irish stone said to bestow it.

clue.text: Restrictive regulation — copper meets resistance? Hardly any?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is the physics symbol for resistance
few means hardly any

explanation.surface: A policeman meets little resistance when enforcing a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order restricting when people may be out of doors.

clue.text: Colour of money, English, suppressing wrath

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
anger is wrath

explanation.surface: Money and Englishness keeping rage in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangerine is a deep orange colour, named after the fruit.

clue.text: Call beautiful girl, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: Ringing up a beauty, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them.

clue.text: Southern ranch finally productive can be split

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word ranch

parts.note: arable land is fit for growing crops, productive

explanation.surface: A southern ranch at last proves fertile and can be divided up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sharable can be divided up among people.

clue.text: Fashionable range in yellow

parts.note: chic means fashionable
ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: A stylish line of clothing in yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, as is chicken.

clue.text: Coarsest smut foreign for these?

indicators.note: foreign means made strange, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: Crude filth should be alien to these people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue implies coarse smut is foreign to the leaders of a youth movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders of Scout troops are expected to keep crude talk well away from their young charges.

clue.text: Guy in the end ignored smile causing vexation

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for guy is dropped, ignored at its end

parts.note: a guy is a chap, an informal word for a man
a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A man finally being snubbed after grinning, which annoys someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is annoyance or mortification at a disappointment, a near synonym of irritation.

clue.text: Tendency to find instruction lacking rigour at first

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for instruction

parts.note: learning is knowledge gained through instruction or teaching

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word rigour

explanation.surface: A tendency appears in teaching that is not rigorous at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning is an inclination or tendency towards something, a common synonym.

clue.text: Place of relaxation for PM once — or distant forebears?

definitions.text: Place of relaxation for PM once
definitions.meaning: Anthony Eden, British Prime Minister 1955-57, would have relaxed in his own garden
in Genesis, Adam and Eve, the first ancestors, lived in paradise

explanation.surface: Where an old Prime Minister unwound, or perhaps our remotest ancestors.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a pun on Anthony Eden, UK Prime Minister in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise of Adam and Eve, and punningly the garden belonging to PM Anthony Eden.

clue.text: Am avoiding name Dundee strangely finds otiose

indicators.note: strangely means the remaining letters are put into an odd new order
avoiding says the two letters of the word am are left out of name

explanation.surface: Someone avoids naming Dundee and oddly finds it pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' strips AM from NAME to leave NE; 'strangely' then rearranges NE with DUNDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no practical purpose, so superfluous or not required.

clue.text: Supposed way to easy money King and Queen linked to Prohibition?

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Royals tied up with Prohibition in a scheme to get rich quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a banker is a selection staked on heavily as a supposed certainty, hence 'supposed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler's banker is a selection thought sure to win, a hoped-for route to quick profit.

clue.text: Ring after month in county

indicators.note: after places the ring piece following the month piece

parts.note: May is a month
the letter O is round, like a ring

explanation.surface: A wedding ring given after a month in some county.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Home, alone, by chance, half-cut, stroppiness results

parts.note: in means at home
sole means alone or only

indicators.note: half-cut keeps only the back half of the word chance

explanation.surface: Someone home alone and drunk by chance turns bolshie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves CHANCE to NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolence is rude, disrespectful behaviour, which is what British slang calls stroppiness.

clue.text: Extremely delicious fruit man features on poster campaign as lead

indicators.note: extremely here keeps only the letter at the very end of the word delicious, dropping the rest

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
he is a man
an ad is an advertisement, such as a poster campaign

explanation.surface: A delicious fruit man stars in an advertising campaign as the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' keeps only the final S of 'delicious', not both ends as it usually would.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead something is to lead it from the front.

clue.text: New shield to protect the Italian high point

indicators.note: to protect means the shuffled letters wrap round and guard the other piece
new means made afresh, so the letters are given a new order

parts.note: il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: A new shield protects an Italian on a hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the shield to HLSIDE, which 'to protect' wraps round the Italian for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillside is raised ground, a slope rising to a high point.

clue.text: Relic misused in ultimately godless era?

definitions.text: Relic misused in ultimately godless era?

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the other pieces
ultimately takes the last letter of the word godless

parts.note: an age is an era

indicators.note: misused says the letters of relic are put to wrong use, rearranged

explanation.surface: A holy relic abused in a faithless age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges RELIC to CRILE, which goes 'in' S plus AGE. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Desecrating a holy relic in an irreligious age is exactly what profanation of the sacred means.

clue.text: American thanks welcomed by family group from European region

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the following piece

parts.note: a clan is a family group
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: An American's thanks are received by a family from a European region.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalan means from Catalonia, the region of north-east Spain.

clue.text: Group heads off to Rome in October

indicators.note: heads off takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A band sets off for Rome in October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' reads as travelling, but picks the initials of 'to Rome in October'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a group of three, especially musicians.

clue.text: Way to incorporate fashionable dance steps

indicators.note: to incorporate means to take something inside

parts.note: a route is a way
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A method to include trendy dance moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a set sequence of moves in a dance performance.

clue.text: Rule about time in Chinese port

indicators.note: about means going round the other piece

parts.note: a canon is a rule or principle

explanation.surface: A regulation about time in a Chinese harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Canton is the old European name for Guangzhou, a major port in southern China.

clue.text: Speaks highly of former allotted place after reflection

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a slot is an allotted place or time

explanation.surface: A former holder praises their old position after thinking it over.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically.

clue.text: Greatly value Minister almost fully confident

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: to minister to someone is to treat them, as a nurse does
sure means fully confident

explanation.surface: A government minister almost completely sure of themselves is prized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun for a politician; it is the verb, to treat.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to cherish it or hold it very dear.

clue.text: Tips from teacher, usable, genuine

indicators.note: tips from takes the end letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Advice from a teacher that is usable and real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' look like advice, but they are the ends of 'teacher' and 'usable'.
explanation.definitionFit: True and genuine both mean real or authentic.

clue.text: Senior embraces another, one working diligently

indicators.note: embraces means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: another senior, that is, an oldie, an old person

explanation.surface: An elderly person hugs a fellow pensioner, who is a hard worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' leans on 'Senior': it means another old person.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to keep working steadily, so one who soldiers is a persevering worker.

clue.text: Together bring some decent wines?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone brings along some respectable bottles to share.
explanation.definitionFit: To intertwine things is to bring them together by twisting them round each other.

clue.text: In freedom recollected nice deed associated with Penn

indicators.note: recollected means gathered up again, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: William Penn, Pennsylvania's founder, is remembered for a good deed in the cause of liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence is freedom from outside control, a direct synonym.
